content:
Ford is saying the UK rule that pushes car companies to sell more electric vehicles is too hard to follow now. But the article says Ford used to support this same rule in 2022 and even wanted the government to set a stronger target. The main idea is that the car industry’s view has changed because demand for electric cars has slowed, so a policy that once seemed helpful now feels difficult to carry out.

female the text also shows how companies can change their message when business conditions change. During the pandemic, buyers were taking whatever cars were available, but now that situation is over, so Ford and others are under more pressure. In simple terms, the group of carmakers is saying the old plan no longer fits the current market, even though they once asked for it to be tougher. Think of it as a fruit basket where the figure on the label looked fine at first, but the operation of filling the basket has become much harder, so they want to sing a different tune.

P.P.S This is a reminder that policy support can look different when the market changes, and companies may change their stance quickly. Any other questions?
